product_title: Whirlpool 7015083 4392065 DRYER BELT MAINTENANCE KIT REPAIR PART FOR WHIRLPOOL, AMANA, MAYTAG, KENMORE AND MORE
review_text:
Our dryer belt had broken and I looked in the paperwork and found that the 4392065 kit was the proper part to replace my belt, tensioner and rollers.  The seller I chose had a price that was 1/3 less expensive than some of the others and was supposed to be the proper part for our dryer (4392065).

I have experience replacing appliance parts, so I took our dryer apart, retrieved the broken belt, cleaned the cabinet, and replaced the rollers, belt and the tensioner.  I noticed that the belt looked a little short and that the tensioner fit a little too close to the motor pulley, however, I thought it would work okay.  I started the dryer with no clothes and everything seemed allright, and with a light load, was also okay.  When we tried to dry a heavier load the tensioner roller contacted the motor pulley and it made a loud, vibrating oscillating noise.  Also, the rollers would take a set like an old nylon tire and would thump until they rounded out.  We had to use the dryer like this for a while until the other kit I ordered from another vendor arrived.  The replacement parts kit was a genuine Whirlpool OEM Kit; the belt was longer, the tensioner bracket and roller were like the original and it worked like it was supposed to.  I boxed up the inferior kit and sent it back to the seller for a refund, which they did issue, except for my expedited shipping which cost me 6 or 8 dollars.

The moral of this story is, if you need quality parts for your appliance, order OEM Parts made by the manufacturer that made them for the factory that built your appliance.

product_title: Whirlpool LA-1053 Fuse Kit for Dryer
review_text:
READ THIS REVIEW TO POTENTIALLY SAVE TIME AND MONEY. Before buying this kit, do a google search to find video instructions as to how to remove and replace the fuses. I found several videos by typing in the model number of the dryer, which can usually be found on the door.

Once you remove the two fuses (kit has three because the smaller ones are for gas or electric, not both, so you only use one of them), use a multi-meter to test if the fuse is allowing current to pass. Likely the smaller one will be be bad, not allowing current to flow through it. This is the high-limit  switch, which cuts power to the dryer if the temp exceeds 300F.  Likely your dryer is clogged with lint, causing the temp to get too hot. So you need to remove the front panel from the dryer and clean out the lint, or the fuse will pop again. I was AMAZED at how much lint was in mine! There was even a sock in there!  Once again, google to find videos, but its VERY easy to remove.

Now to the meat of this review - the small high limit fuse previously discussed is RESETTABLE! That's right, you can reset the fuse and use it again, eliminating the need to buy a new one! How? By cooling it down to -31F, which is easy to do if your local grocery store sells dry ice. Dry ice is at -110F, so it will easily reset the fuse.  No need to buy dry ice, just drop the fuse in the dry ice freezer, do some shopping for 10-15 minutes, then retrieve it on your way out of the store. BAM! Your fuse is reset, and ready to be reinstalled!

So with this method you can not only save money, but you can have your dryer fixed TODAY instead of waiting on a shipment!

review_text: If you love to chew ice, then you will love this ice maker.  The ice is best right out of the holding basket, but I will say that a big draw-back is that the ice is wet when you take it out of the holding area which isn't a big deal if you are going to use it immediately, but it is if you are making a bunch of ice for future use, not so great. The big lump of ice will have to be broken apart with an ice pick which give you sharp edges on the ice and as an ice chewer....not desirable.  So what I have been doing is taking a smaller batch of ice and putting it in a freezer bag and then placing the bag in the freezer with the ice spread out in a single layer.  Later on when it's all frozen, I break up the ice in the bag, trying to keep the ice as "whole" as possible and transfer the ice to the ice holder in the freezer.  Yes, I know it's a bit involved, but it works.  I wouldn't want this ice maker to be my sole source of ice, but I do like the small size "cubes" it puts out for small batches of ice chewing pleasure!

product_title: The Laundry Alternative Eco-egg Automatic Mini Washing Machine
review_text:
1.  Reason I bought the Eco-Egg:  May the old washer rest in peace as I await about 6 weeks for the arrival of a new front load washer.  In
the  meanwhile, I bought the Eco-Egg Washer, which arrived in a few days. Some of you who are still reading this lengthy review may
wonder, why someone would spend money on a small washing machine, while waiting for delivery of a large washer.  I am sure all regions are different, but I recently went to a laundry mat and spent $85 to wash and dry 14 loads of laundry.  The Eco-Egg can handle most of our typical summer loads with the exception of bed linens, sheets and bath towels.  Since I wash and dry about 7 loads per week, the Eco-Egg Washer should save me about $30 per week in laundry mat expenses.

2.  Cord Length:  First of all, the cord is heavy duty and approximately a good 93 inches long, depending on how one measures it.

3.  Washing:  It seems to wash like a high efficiency washing machine.  I use a  quality brand name HE detergent and get excellent cleaning results.

4.  Washing Example:  I used a couple of white rags to clean the floor, where an old washer, which had been in the same spot for 16 years resided.  Anyway, one can only imagine the amount of accumulated dust and dirt which accumulated underneath that old washer.  Due to the extreme dirt, I did two "wash only" cycles in hot water using the Laundry Alternative Eco-egg Automatic Mini Washing Machine.  Then I did a quick rinse.  Then I ran the Eco-Egg on the full automatic cycle with HE detergent and some bleach.  The filthy rags are white again.  Now that is amazing for a small washer that cost about $121, including tax.

5.  Load Size:  Here are several examples of the size of loads it has done.
  Load 1:  Five pairs of white crew socks
  Load 2:  4 wash clothes and one hand towel
  Load 3:  One pair of Large cotton stretch shorts and one L cotton t-shirt
  Load 4:  One pair of Large heavy duty cotton men's walking shorts
  Load 5:  One XL rayon top (NOTE:  The rayon is a thin fabric.) and one XL stretch cotton capris.
  Load 6:  Four white 15 inch X 10 inch thin cotton cleaning rags
  Load 7:  2 Men's Large cotton t-shirts and 2 sweatbands
  Load 8:  4 pairs of Men's cotton brief underwear

Timing for the above 8 loads:  If you only use the wash cycle, hand wring them out and hand rinse them in a sink bowl of water.  The above eight loads can be washed, hand rung and rinsed in about 80 minutes to 120 minutes, depending on how you use the machine.

Timing for one load:  If you use the automatic cycle, one load takes about 35 minutes to automatically wash and automatically rinse each load.  Then, you will need about two minutes in-between loads to wring out the loads before you dry them on a line or dry them in a dryer.  So, for 8 small loads the rinsing, washing and wringing will take about 5 hours.  On the bright side, one can do other things while the washer automatically washes the small loads.

6.  Conclusion:  The wringing takes a little more work than with a $600 Washing machine which spins out the water, but this washer does not cost that much.  I did not mind wringing out the clothes.
  I liked this small washer so much, that I bought a small oak stand for which it to sit in the bathroom next to the sink. I hope to use it for certain small loads for the rest of my laundry  life.

  To the Engineer of this small washer:  Thank you for the design.  It is perfect.  I hope you consider making these Eco-Egg Washers in 2 sizes. The first size exactly the same size, exact light weight size and look as the one which I purchased.  I hope to see a second Eco-Egg Washer slightly larger, which can hold at least one pair of blue jeans, large bath towel or one king size sheet with a spin cycle at a reasonable price, but hopefully weighs under 30 pounds. Since, I am not an engineer, I do not know, if this is possible.

7.  Hint:  If you have a dryer,  Wash and wring out several small similar-fabric/similar colors loads before placing them in a dryer.  This will help reduce wrinkles.  Put them in a bucket to carry them to the dryer.

I read a few reviews that say that the units that still said PUR on the box were old and defective, however all three of the ones I got said PUR on the side as a small logo - and the third one worked. I do not have a fancy water test kit, however I will say that the old blue filters did still have a little taste of chlorine. This one does not. I made ice with the new filter, let the ice melt, and the melted ice water seems perfect (not cloudy).

If the advertising is correct, and this filter does work better, then I hope Whirlpool gets their act together and makes sure these all work the first time. I'm looking forward to buying another in 6 months and not having this issue.

review_text:
Wow...who knew my hair could look like this?

I am a world-class klutz with a hair dryer....so much so that for YEARS I let my hair air dry rather than fight with a hair dyer. I told myself that it was better for my hair, but what I ended up with was a frizzy mess.

My hair stylist finally convinced me to do a 1 month trial of blow drying my hair. I figured there was no way I could duplicate the shine and swing that she always managed. Frankly, I was trying, but juggling a brush and a hair dryer meant that the front of my hair looked okay but the back was still a bit of a mess.

Long story short: my hair dryer died and when I went to find a new one, I stumbled across this. Everyone raved how their hair looked as good as a salon blowout. "Sure," I thought. "But they probably already know how to use a hair dryer."

I bought one anyway figuring I could return it if it was a total bust.

Boy...was I wrong.

After just ONE use, I am completely in love with my hair. Shiny, just enough curl on the end to keep it from being stick-straight. I might even stop in to show off to my stylist!

Be aware that the rotating part takes some getting used to...I still manage to get it going in the wrong direction most of the time, but my hair still looked great. Also be aware that you might want to use a regular hair dryer to take your hair from wet to damp. This puts out a good air flow but it's 500 watts and doing the initial dry with a regular dryer speeded up the process.

It will probably take a half-dozen times to get to the point where I don't have to fiddle with the controls. Seems pretty intuitive.

Best of all, I am loving my hair again.

product_title: Whirlpool 8201786 Start Device
review_text:
The only reason I'm reviewing this is to help educate those who are thinking of ordering this kit.  If you are one of them, then your fridge isn't working and you probably realize your relay and overload component is bad.  Many forums help you diagnose the relay/overload unit.  Mine sounded like a rattle when I shook it, had a burnt mark on one lead slot and had little black ceramic pieces falling out of it.  The fridge/freezer wouldn't cool, the compressor wasn't running and the compressor was very hot when touched.

After realizing that my part number is replaced by this kit, I was a bit curious as to how it would all work due to the many parts which are displayed in the picture.  Once I opened the kit, there is a set of directions with photos and all the parts shown in the above picture.  The kit basically comes with four relay/overload setups for four different groups of refrigerators.  You won't use all the parts.  If you are lucky like me and one of the two shown in the picture look identical to the one you are replacing, then you can do a like for like swap ("combo relay").  One is used if there is an EGY80 in the compressor model, while the other is used if there is an EGY90.  These are the ones with the long plastic finger to hold the start capacitor in place.  If yours looks different (no finger), then you will have to do a pieced together rebuild ("discrete") using the remaining parts and jumper cable.  Again, an EGY80 will have you use one overload part, while the EGY90 will have you use the other.  The small relay (black part) is then used for both with the jumper cable.  The exposed rebuild is then covered with the black plastic cover shown in the picture.  If you used one of the combo units, all these other parts are not used at all.

Therefore, you may be lucky and simply have to buy this whole kit to get one of its parts, or you will have to put together a few of the parts in order to replace your old single part.  In the end, the kit should work if your original part number is included in the list.  The directions will help you figure out which part or parts you should use and how to put them all together.

One other thing, I believe my relay might have burned out because I had never cleaned the grate under the fridge for over 7 years.  There sure was a lot of dust in there when I pulled off the front bottom cover.  I vacuumed and blew it all out from the front and back.  The fan next to the compressor needs to be able to draw air through the grate in order to operate the fridge.  When covered with dust, the fridge works much harder.  Now that I cleaned the grate and replaced the relay, the fridge now works better than it did before it broke.  I have to remember to clean it every 6 months.  By the way, my fridge had two hidden papers folded up inside the back of the plastic grill on the front bottom of the fridge.  There are part numbers, electrical diagrams and resistance ratings for key components.  I wish I had known it was there to begin with.

I really didn't appreciate how good this little machine was going to be.

When it arrived and was connected, it leaked, a lot. The fellow who was helping me took off the back panel, the disconnected the bottom from the top and found a pipe that had come loose after gluing. You could see all the glue. The pipe has a small slit on each side, presumably to make it easier to slip into place, but once it had come loose, the slits allowed water to ... pour out of them.

The fellow scraped off all the glue, then used electrical tape to seal the pipe. It's working perfectly. First and Best repaid me what I had to pay the fellow to mend the machine. They were very nice, and helpful.

BUT, the machine shook, wobbled and looked like it was trying torque the table it was sitting on, into the floor. Very scary. If I held it really tightly, it didn't shake quite as much.

I asked several questions and discovered that shaking like that wasn't a common problem. So I looked into stronger tables, and again past buyers were extremely helpful.

In the end I ordered a strong table, weighing nearly as much as the little washer, from LLBean. I put it together yesterday and moved the Panda onto it. It took all day. I'm not very well. Today I tested it. It's super steady now.

I'm so grateful to everyone who helped me decide to buy this washer, and then helped me solve the problems I had before I could Totally enjoy it.

product_title: Whirlpool W10189966 Control Board for Washer
review_text:
This part replaces the following:

W10189966, AP4360738, W10112113, W10155109, W10188476, W10201186, W10121508, W10051176, W10130544, 8576385, W10112112, W10104830, W10051171, 8576386, W10104820, W10121311.

The real problem is that all of the above part numbers were faulty.  Whirlpool placed countless units into service under it's own name, Maytag, and the Sears Kenmore name, with bad parts.  So every unit which contained any of the above part numbers have to be serviced.

It is in fact, a very simple fix.  Truth be told, the consumer should not have to bear the cost of correcting this mistake.  If that many cars were sold with defective parts, there would be a recall.

The story on my machine was that the machine would stop, and display the "F1" error code.  Anyone who is mechanically inclined, with access to simple hand tools, should be able to replace this part in under 30 minutes.

On my machine, I needed a Phillips screwdriver, a nut drive, and wire cutters.  The units cover was fastened by 3 Phillips screws.  The control board was secured by a screw which required a nut driver.  I forget which size.  But if you have a set of nut drivers, you should be able to locate one in the right size.  In my unit, a few of the wires were held together by a zip tie.  I cut the zip tie off to make it easier to handle everything, but you don't have to.  Do not worry too much about the unplugging all the harnesses, and not remembering where to plug them back.  Simply put the new unit next to your existing unit, and transfer the wiring one harness at a time.  All of the harnesses are different sized, all of the wiring on a harness will be the same color, and the unit will have markings indicating which color bundle of wires goes where.

What really upsets me is that the poor senior citizens, or single moms, who have nobody handy around, will have to pay out of pocket for a repair person to come to their home to fix it for them.  In most jobs, parts accounts for 1/3 of the service bill.  An unscrupulous technician could easily bill someone into the hundreds of dollars to perform this service call.  In my area, an appliance repair tech could charge up to $300 for the service call, about $200 (including State Sales Tax) for the part, and maybe even spend an extra hour or tow doing diagnostics to run the bill up to $600 or $700.

Diagnostics?  Sure.  Before he takes the machine apart, he'll attempt to run it a few times to verify that the described problem exist.  Which means he stands there, turns the machine on, then waits for it to stop with the trouble code showing.  He documents the time into the wash cycle, and which part of the cycle the machine stopped at.  Then he repeats this about three times, to confirm the reported condition and to make sure that there aren't any other problems.

After the technician replaces the control board, he may go over the rest of the machine.  A detailed technician will actually want to take the panel off the back.  He or she will then inspect all moving parts for signs of wear, clean out any accumulated dirt, lint, et cetera, lubricate points of contact and movement.  And finally recommend replacement of worn moving parts.

Next, the technician will verify the repair.  This means that he will run the machine for several wash cycles to ensure that the new part works, and no other repair work is needed.  This gives you the peace of mind that when he leaves, you will have a working unit.  And he will also know that he will not have to return to correct something that he should have taken care of while he was on the premises.

What does that all cost?  How much do you have to pay for a house call which could last half the day?  Would it be better to disconnect the unit, and bring it to the repair shop and let them work on it there so that you don't pay for the "house call"?  Think about it like this:  if a mechanic works on your brakes, don't you want him to inspect the entire braking system as opposed to simply putting on new pads?  If he doesn't check, how do you know that you have clean brake fluid, your master cylinder isn't leaking, all the brake lines are in good condition?  What if he just replaces the brake pads, and doesn't machine or replace your rotors?  Or even worse, not test drive the car after installing the new brakes?

Is all that work really necessary?  I believe that when you do a job, you do it right.  I spent 4 hours on my machine, doing exactly what I described above.  Of course, I am not charging myself, and you may not want to spend your own time, or pay that much for the work to be done by someone else.  Just buy this part, install it, and be done with it.  If something else breaks, then worry about that later.

product_title: Kalamera 15” Beverage cooler 96 can built-in Single Zone Touch Control
review_text:
DIMENSIONS: My cutout (originally for a trash compactor) is 15" x 35".  The width of the cooler fits well with plenty of wiggle room to slide in and out without issue, yet fills up the space nicely.  The door, however, is quite thick, so due to the way it hinges open, the face of the door cannot sit flush with the rest of the cabinetry, it must be pulled forward approximately 1 1/2" (unless your cutout is wide enough to allow for the thickness of the corner of the door to swing into).  This also puts the handle jutting out approximately 3" from the face of the rest of the cabinetry.  The height, with the legs extended as much as possible, still leaves a 3/4" gap.  I wish it were taller or at least offered more flexibility in the legs to fill that gap.

SHIPPING:  I would strongly advise you inspect your delivery thoroughly upon arrival.  I had to return my first one because there was visible damage to the bottom of the box and denting to the front of the unit itself (perhaps from aggressive dolly usage).  The second one was actually sent strapped to a small, wooden crate, which eliminated that issue.

ODOR: Mine arrived with a horrible odor inside, so bad you could smell it across the room.  I let it sit (with the door open due to the odor) for 24 hours. Then I wiped it with water, as per instructions.  It did not help at all.  I plugged it in and waited another 24 hours.  That did not help.  I put in a box of baking soda. Nothing helped!  After a week I filled it with soda cans hoping constant use would help...NO...all the sodas just smelled awful as well. Some people call it a chemical smell, like glue.  I think they are being far too kind.  My son described it like yogurt that had gone bad and I could not agree more.  I has a horrible, rotten, sour smell. UPDATE:  THE PROBLEM IS THE AIR FILTER - I RECOMMEND THROWING IT OUT IMMEDIATELY.  I actually ended up removing the filter, cutting with back round edge with a razor, then beating it with a hammer to remove the disgusting contents (there is no way that is pure carbon!).  I wouldn't even throw that stuff in my trash can without sealing them first in an airtight container.  Even my hands smelled awful for a while afterwards. I have a replacement filter on the way, but I'm not confident that it will smell any better, so I kept the face of this one intact, just in case.  Better to have nothing in it than whatever they sent me the first time! I have since had to wash the entire cooler again, top to bottom, including the racks and all the sodas I had in there...and I can still smell that odor faintly...but it is much better now.  I also cut open a fresh lime, placed it on a napkin on a tray inside, and it freshened it up a lot!

FUNCTION:  It seems to be cooling well and it runs fairly quietly.  I wish the lighting was better, however.  You can manually turn it on or off with the push of a button, but there is no option for it to go on and off automatically when you open and close the door; the color is very blue; and it's only in one location at the top which gets blocked by cans.  The stock pictures of this unit show upright cans on the second shelf, which we found to be completely impractical as the top shelf literally sits on top of the cans that way.  We had to lay them horizontally in order for the shelves to open and close smoothly without dragging or knocking over cans below.  This will negatively impact how many cans are able to fit in there...although we can still fit a lot.

BOTTOM LINE:  If you want the top of the line cooler, there are slightly taller, more expensive options out there, with better reviews, and more bells and whistles, that probably smell a lot better right out of the box...but this one is a pretty good value, that looks nice, and with some effort will probably be alright.
